name: Blockchain Fundamentals & Distributed Systems
description: Fundamental concepts of distributed ledgers, peer-to-peer networking, state transition systems, UTXO vs Account models, and cryptographic primitives.

subskills.name: Distributed Ledger Technology Foundations
subskills.description: Understanding append-only distributed ledgers, immutability, cryptographic chaining, and centralized vs decentralized paradigms.

subskills.name: Decentralization Principles & Game Theory
subskills.description: Nakamoto consensus principles, censorship resistance, game theoretic alignment, and permissionless network participation.

subskills.name: Block Architecture & Header Structures
subskills.description: Internal structure of blocks: block header, nonce, difficulty target, timestamp, state root, receipt root, and previous block hash.

subskills.name: UTXO vs Account-Based State Models
subskills.description: Comparison between Bitcoin's Unspent Transaction Output (UTXO) model and Ethereum's Account/Nonce state model.

subskills.name: P2P Networking & Gossip Protocols
subskills.description: Peer-to-peer communication, node discovery (Kademlia DHT, discv4/discv5), and transaction/block propagation via gossip protocols.

subskills.name: Transaction Lifecycle & Mempool Dynamics
subskills.description: Transaction creation, digital signature verification, mempool propagation, MEV dynamics, replacement-by-fee (RBF), and block inclusion.

subskills.name: Cryptographic Hashing & Merkle Trees
subskills.description: SHA-256, Keccak-256, RIPEMD-160, Merkle Trees, Merkle Patricia Tries, and cryptographic proof verification (Merkle proofs).

subskills.name: Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) Theory
subskills.description: The Byzantine Generals Problem, crash fault tolerance vs Byzantine fault tolerance, safety vs liveness, and 33%/51% attack thresholds.

subskills.name: Blockchain Trilemma & Tradeoff Analysis
subskills.description: Analyzing the fundamental tradeoffs between Decentralization, Security, and Scalability across L1 and L2 architectures.

github.signal: Cryptographic hash functions, Merkle tree implementations, and block parsing scripts
Raw transaction serialization, signature validation, and mempool listeners
P2P node setup, gossip config, or consensus simulation scripts

cv.signal: Demonstrated deep understanding of distributed ledger mechanics, Merkle proofs, and consensus economics
Architected low-latency mempool monitors and evaluated BFT consensus models against blockchain trilemma constraints

linkedin.signal: Endorsements and publications in Blockchain Architecture, Distributed Systems, and Cryptography

assessment.signal: Passes comprehensive blockchain fundamentals assessment covering Merkle proofs, mempool dynamics, BFT theory, and Trilemma tradeoffs

junior.description: Understands block header layouts, UTXO vs Account balance models, and fundamental decentralization principles.

mid.description: Constructs and verifies Merkle inclusion proofs, analyzes mempool transaction propagation, and understands P2P gossip networks.

senior.description: Evaluates BFT consensus resilience under adversary conditions and models architectural tradeoffs across the blockchain trilemma.
